texts: On day 510 of Year 2, a cold wind blew off the sea for two weeks in midwinter.
Every lantern on the Cliff Path held through the two weeks.
Keepers on the Cliff Path refilled the mire-essence at midnight and at the third watch.
Keepers on the Cliff Path used extra salt-bloom per lantern.
The Council raised the salt-bloom ration by ten percent for the two weeks.
A handful of nightmoths flew in the cold wind each night.
The thread harvest on the Cliff Path was steady through the two weeks.
Cauldron Hall distilled at its normal cadence.

parse: (: s2_lantern_rule (Implication (And (Member $x lantern) (On $x cliff_path)) (And (Member (sk_hold $x) hold) (Experiencer (sk_hold $x) $x) (Past (sk_hold $x)) (Measure (sk_hold $x) duration 2 week))) (STV 1.0 0.9))

q1_issues.issue: (Degree sk_salt_bloom_1 quantity extra) fills the quantity-scale level slot with 'extra', which is not one of the three fixed construction markers (excessive / sufficient / insufficient) that scale licenses.

(Per sk_use_1 lantern) hangs the per-lantern rate on the using event, but 'per lantern' measures the amount of salt-bloom, not the event, and an unnumbered rate has no licensed carrier (rates exist only as compound units inside a Measure).

'through the two weeks' inside the lantern rule (and 'for the two weeks' at statements 47 and 62) becomes (Measure e duration 2 week), which states the extent but drops the anaphoric identity of the one two-week span sentences 2, 6 and 8 all point back to.

q2_gaps: anaphoric definite temporal-interval NP ('through/for the two weeks') referring back to a previously stated span - only calendar terms, deictics, durations and During-over-an-eventuality are provided, so the shared interval cannot be one referent
unmeasured rate / distributive 'per N' modifier on a quantity ('extra salt-bloom per lantern') - a rate is defined only as a <unit>_per_<unit> compound inside a Measure, which needs a number

unmeasured comparative quantity modifier ('extra N' = more than the usual amount) - an elided-standard comparative, for which the instruction set supplies no form, and the Degree quantity markers are a closed set of three
an ordinal-named clock period as a time point ('at the third watch') - no rule says whether it is a named-time constant or a definite witness with an Ordinal atom
a day-of-year date in a non-Gregorian calendar ('day 510 of Year 2') - (Day n) / (Year n) accept the integers, but the seeded calendar-ordering machinery assumes day-of-month numbering

whether a vague-quantity group with a distributive predicate ('a handful of nightmoths flew') takes the per-member (PartOf $x g) rule: Cardinality's 'Several birds sang' example omits it while Quantifiers lists 'several dogs barked' as taking it
review.notes: Otherwise a careful parse: the every-lantern universal, the Cliff Path / Cauldron Hall name+kind atoms, the compound genus atoms and the copular-with-time-modifier dual-emit in sentence 8 all match the instruction set. 'Per' is counted as licensed here only because it is the preposition actually used.

issues.reason: Degree's level slot is specified to record the surface word that was used and not to be collapsed into a band, the three fixed markers being named only because they select how a following infinitive is encoded, so (Degree sk_salt_bloom_1 quantity extra) is truthful, well-typed improvisation in uncovered territory rather than a false, ill-typed or over-asserted atom.

The preposition-named oblique licence covers this exactly - a PP answering none of where/when/how/whence/whither takes the preposition actually used as its head - so (Per sk_use_1 lantern) is licensed, and the claim that a rate can only live as a <unit>_per_<unit> compound inside a Measure ignores that residual licence; VP-level attachment of a distributive per-phrase to the event is not false.

(Measure e duration 2 week) is the instruction set's own encoding for a 'for'-duration and is entailed by 'held / was steady through the two weeks', so nothing false or wider than the text reaches the KB - the lost identity of the single two-week span is a coverage gap (the reviewer's own q2 gap 1), not a parse defect.

gaps_confirmed: no carrier for an anaphoric definite temporal-interval NP ('through / for the two weeks') - the one span the passage keeps pointing back at cannot be a referent
an unmeasured distributive rate ('extra salt-bloom per lantern') has no carrier beyond the bare surface-preposition oblique - the <unit>_per_<unit> Measure form needs a number
'extra N' - an unmeasured, elided-standard quantity comparative has no licensed form, and the Degree quantity markers are a closed set of three
'at the third watch' - an ordinal-named clock period: named-time constant vs definite witness plus Ordinal is undecided
'day 510 of Year 2' - day-of-year dating in a non-Gregorian calendar; (Day n) takes the integer but the seeded ordering machinery presumes day-of-month

whether a vague-quantity group with a distributive predicate takes the per-member (PartOf $x g) rule - Cardinality's 'Several birds sang' omits it while the same section mandates it for 'Both dogs barked'
new_gaps: 'through <interval>' has no licensed head: During is restricted to during / while / throughout ('never a synonym head'), so a throughout-style PP over a named span can only fall back on a duration Measure

past-tense habitual: a frequency adjunct on a finite past clause ('a handful of nightmoths flew ... each night') - Frequency & habitual says the event stays unmarked, but the clause carries past tense, and no rule says whether (Past e) may stand beside (Every e 1 day)

the rule-vs-no-rule question above also has no example for a bare-plural episodic group subject with neither count nor quantifier ('Keepers on the Cliff Path refilled the mire-essence') - the bare-plural-episodic rule gives a group witness and stops
adjudication.notes: All three issues are coverage-gap reports rather than rule violations: every atom emitted for 'extra', 'per lantern' and the two-week span is true of the text, uses a licensed head, and asserts no more than the sentence states. One unflagged minor point, left as acceptable: 'Northcove' gets a Name but no type atom, defensible for a solid-spelling name whose kind word is not separately stated.
